summary: Refuse settings reads and writes of the device-credential rows (deviceSessions, devicePairingCode, mobilePairing.*, pushTokens, opencode.env.*, google.clientSecret) to a device session without the admin scope, at the same frame gate both remote hosts enforce.

desktop.reason: The desktop renderer reaches settings through ElectronIpcHost, which applies no device scopes, and a desktop dialing a remote backend authenticates with the backend token, which carries FULL_SCOPES. No desktop UI or behaviour changes.

reactNativeIos.reason: apps/mobile reads and writes only the chat default mode, default model and default instance settings through settings:get and settings:set. None of those keys is in a protected family, so the phone sees no change.

nativeAndroid.reason: apps/android reads only the default model and default instance settings (NewSessionCoordinator). None of those keys is in a protected family, so the app sees no change.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema change and no migration. The rows stay where they are; only who may reach them through the settings channels changes.

updateRelease.reason: No package identity, signing, deep link, update channel or wire format change. The refusal uses the existing 'not permitted: protected setting' error frame.

automated: tests/unit/settings-device-auth-gate.test.ts drives a real WsHost: a chat-scoped device is refused settings:get, settings:set and settings:remove on every protected key, and the handler never runs; an admin-scoped device is allowed; ordinary keys stay open. The chat-scoped case failed before the fix (settings:set deviceSessions returned ok).
The same file iterates ADMIN_ONLY_SETTING_FAMILIES and pins its exact contents, so a dropped entry fails.
notExercised: Not exercised against a real paired phone; the phone apps do not use any protected key.
